messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis of test `testInfiniteLoop`
Details: The test `testInfiniteLoop` invokes `HelpFormatter.printHelp("app", options)` with a width set to 20. The call chain leads to `printHelp(PrintWriter pw, int width, String cmdLineSyntax, String header, Options options, int leftPad, int descPad, String footer, boolean autoUsage)`, which then calls `printUsage(pw, width, cmdLineSyntax, options)` among other things. Inside `printUsage`, an option usage string is constructed, and finally, `printWrapped(pw, width, offset, buff.toString())` is called to print the usage text with wrapping.

`printWrapped` calls `renderWrappedText(StringBuffer sb, int width, int nextLineTabStop, String text)`. This method attempts to wrap the text according to the specified width. The wrapping logic finds a wrap position and appends the trimmed substring to the buffer. It then pads following lines and continues to find wrap positions within a loop.

The problem occurs in `renderWrappedText`. If the wrap position returned by `findWrapPos` is equal to the previous wrap position (`pos == lastPos`), a `RuntimeException` is thrown to prevent an infinite loop. This exception message references "[CLI-162]", indicating that this is a known issue.

Because the test used to hang and crash and now throws this exception instead, it shows that the wrap position calculation can yield conditions where no progress is made (wrap position doesn't advance), causing an infinite loop scenario. This arises likely because the text to wrap or the width setting causes `findWrapPos` to not find a proper wrap position that progresses.

The infinite loop/failure can be attributed to `renderWrappedText` failing to correctly wrap at certain widths/texts, resulting in an unchanging wrap position and the infinite loop detection being triggered.

The best place to fix the issue would be in `renderWrappedText` and potentially in `findWrapPos` (not shown here) to ensure it always returns a valid wrap position progressing the split to avoid infinite loops.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer,int,int,java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
